verdict.rationale: Factory documents several product-run ways to execute agents without the user standing up a backend. Agents run in Factory App web sessions, Linear and Jira issues can be delegated directly to Factory, Droid Computers keep state between sessions, and a Sessions API creates and drives Droid sessions. However, no item explicitly says Factory hosts and manages the compute; the Droid Computers evidence quoted only covers Bring Your Own Machine, which is self-managed. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of Factory-hosted managed cloud compute, details on scaling and parallel cloud execution, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can use a managed cloud offering to run agents without operating my own backend infrastructure

citations.quote: Run the /readiness-report slash command in a Factory App web or desktop session
Assign a Linear issue to Factory or mention `@Factory` in an issue comment to have Droid investigate, implement, and test the work.
Droid Computers **retain state**: installed packages, files, running services, and configuration all persist between sessions.
Create and drive Droid sessions: manage their lifecycle, settings, and messages.
